routes.name: Visa-free tourist admission
routes.summary: Citizens of many countries, including the US, Canada, the UK, the Netherlands and most of Europe, can visit without a visa. Standard admission is 30 days. US citizens can stay up to 90 days and Dutch nationals up to 180 days.

other: The page gives no full visa-free list. Check with DIMAS or the Netherlands Worldwide Caribbean visa pages.
Everyone needs an approved online ED Card, up to 7 days before departure.
Passport must be valid for the whole stay and issued within the last 10 years.
Admission is decided by immigration at the port of entry.

stay.note: US citizens up to 90 days, Dutch nationals up to 180 consecutive days. Extensions must be approved before the stay ends.

fees.label: Sustainability fee for air arrivals, collected via ED Card

sources.label: Aruba Tourism Authority: Entry requirements and visas

routes.name: Caribbean visa (short stay)
routes.summary: Travelers from countries that need a visa for Aruba apply for a Caribbean visa through the Dutch system. It does not allow travel to the Schengen Area. Some people with certain residence permits or visas are exempt.

other: Exact exemptions, fees and processing times were not confirmed on an official page. Check DIMAS and Netherlands Worldwide.
An ESTA does not count as a US visa for exemption purposes.

sources.label: Aruba Tourism Authority: Entry requirements and visas

routes.name: Airport and cruise transit
routes.summary: Airport transit passengers may skip the visa if they stay in the international transit area from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM with onward travel documents. Cruise stopovers of 24 hours or less generally need no visa.

sources.label: Aruba Tourism Authority: Entry requirements and visas

routes.name: Work and residence permits (DIMAS)
routes.summary: DIMAS handles residence and work permits under the National Ordinance on Admission and Expulsion. Directors of companies who don't meet the conditions for living, working and starting a business in Aruba need a work permit. Permit types, fees and PR timelines were not confirmed.

other: Details not confirmed on an official page. See the gobierno.aw Work and residence permit page and DIMAS.
